_comment: End-to-End pipeline configuration. No secrets live here — the SSH password is read from $PHORVEX_SSH_PASSWORD or ~/.phorvex-e2e/secret, and the console bearer token from $PHORVEX_CONSOLE_TOKEN or ~/.phorvex-e2e/console-token.
_console_comment: The IN-CLUSTER console, reached over the authenticated endpoint DevOps provisions (see
_auth_comment below), never the Cognito ALB. This used to point at localhost:8095 on
the jump host — a systemd service running a binary built from a loose, un-versioned
copy of the source. That stack was never built by CI and never deployed by ArgoCD, so
the suite was asserting contracts against code nobody could trace to a commit.
The console now runs as a container inside the operator's pod and streams the audit
the operator actually writes, so what this tests is what ArgoCD deployed.

_auth_comment: The console authenticates every request except /api/health (docs/CONSOLE-AUTH.md).
mode=http sends real HTTP from the transport host to `base` and, with auth=bearer,
carries the console credential the deployed verifier checks. The credential is NEVER
in this file: it comes from $PHORVEX_CONSOLE_TOKEN (the CI secret) or from the private
0600 file named by token_file / $PHORVEX_CONSOLE_TOKEN_FILE — exactly one of them.
It travels to curl on stdin, never in argv, a URL or a retained error.
`base` is provisioned by DevOps and comes from $PHORVEX_CONSOLE_BASE (or set it here):
an HTTPS endpoint that reaches the console verifier with normal certificate checks
(ca_file / $PHORVEX_CONSOLE_CA_FILE names a CA bundle ON THE TRANSPORT HOST for a
private CA), or plain HTTP to a loopback address on the transport host — the SSH jump
host in ssh mode — i.e. a tunnel DevOps owns there. Anything else is refused before a
request is made. Redirects are never followed, so a Cognito login redirect is an error
rather than a leaked credential. Missing base/credential fails preflight closed.
mode=kubectl-proxy (the previous default) reaches the in-cluster Service through the
API server. It authenticates the kubectl user to the API SERVER and carries no console
credential, so since the identity boundary every protected route answers 401 through
it. It remains only as an explicit anonymous compatibility path (PHORVEX_CONSOLE_MODE).
`lens` is a presentation hint the console may use to narrow a view; it is not identity.

_bounds_comment: The stream is framed incrementally now, so these bound TRAFFIC and RETAINED RECORDS
rather than one buffer holding the whole window. Full decision traces exhausted 8 MB
in ~36s on EKS, which aborted the 51s live observation at the old 16 MB buffer cap.
max_bytes is the total the reader will pull before declaring the window unobservable
within its budget; max_records bounds what is kept in memory after scope filtering;
max_frame_bytes bounds one unterminated frame. Reaching any of them is an explicit
failure — the run reports an incomplete observation, never a shorter successful one.
capture._clock_skew_comment: Record timestamps come from the operator's clock and the injection time from the pipeline's. Records within this many seconds before the injection are still considered part of the post window; what makes one attributable is A05's event/target UID binding, not its position in the window.
_namespaces_comment: "target": capture only the namespace this run took a baseline and a policy for, which
is the only namespace it can verify anything about. null makes the cluster-wide claim
(the default for an untargeted observe run). A list names namespaces explicitly.
Whichever it is, the run document records it and a scoped run is never reported as

invariants._law_reason_prefixes: A law's Verdict.Reason does not always start with its Name() — e.g. availability-floor writes 'availability:'. These are the literal prefixes in internal/feasibility/*.go, so the check matches the code instead of guessing.
_action_log_evidence_comment: Command-specific log patterns for the actions whose only independent evidence is the
workload's own log. Each is a Python regex, matched ONLY against lines the pod wrote
after the action started (kubectl --since-time) and only while the pod still carries
the UID observed before the action.
kv-reset uses vLLM's own API name for the operation. adapter-rotate is deliberately
ABSENT: 'lora' matches vLLM's startup banner and its configuration dump, so it
confirmed an adapter rotation that never happened. Until someone reviews the exact
line the deployed vLLM writes on an adapter load/unload and adds it here, an
adapter-rotate is reported as unverifiable rather than confirmed by a generic word.

_targets_comment: litellm, mock-rag-chatbot and phorvex-live-demo were removed from the cluster — ArgoCD now owns that capacity. voicebot replaces them as the stateless rotate target: it already carries r6th.io/rotation-target=true and a voice-defense PhorvexPolicy.

_comment: The operator that WRITES the audit the console streams. Its kill-switch gauge is what
distinguishes a decision-only mirror from a broken actuator (check A06).
It is now the in-cluster operator, whose metrics port has no Service and no ingress —
correctly, since nothing about an operator's internals belongs on the internet. It is
read through the API server's pod proxy instead, using the same kubeconfig the
ground-truth kubectl calls already use. The pod is resolved by label at scrape time,
because it is recreated on every deploy.
